translation: Water diminished and people left the settlement. No one lived there, and no one remembered why. A woodworker went there and first treated the abandoned place as a thing. The woodworker cut a bounded portion of a house's timber, took it, and made a sound new house. On returning, the woodworker took much more; the old roof split open, and a doorway made from the later timber would not fit. The woodworker returned with a child. Rain entered; water lived in the old house. The child referred to the settlement as PERSON and asked, “Water lives in the old house. Who restores the roof?” The woodworker understood and then also used PERSON reference. The roof and doorway were mended; the roof was restored to the settlement under SOCIAL personhood, hearth-fire was renewed, and the child spoke an old name to the place. The path grew. Thereafter people habitually took only bounded portions while restoring the roof, renewing the hearth, and speaking the old name.
notes: Phase 2a place-personhood regression. Controlled human MOVE is ERG+A while rain entry is inactive ABS+U. Child-led PERSON reference precedes adult recognition. Physical MEND and relational RESTORE remain distinct, while continued use survives under reciprocal maintenance.

translation: Rain and wind were heavy. A person lost the path and entered a house. A person of the house gave food to the traveler, who remained there. The traveler told a story and promised the child. At the hearth the child addressed the traveler. First: “Who told the traveler?” An old person had told the traveler: no one can travel the old path; a traveler stays in the house, and food is customarily given to the traveler. Second: “What did the traveler not say?” The traveler had promised the old person and did not tell the old story, then claimed the traveler had not seen the settlement. The child recognized the old person's tool and saw the traveler holding it. Third, the child repeated, “The traveler did not see the settlement,” and asked, “Who went carrying the old person's tool?” The guest was the person in the story: the traveler had seen the settlement. The whole message was then repeated: the old path was unsafe, a traveler was to remain under the roof, and food was owed to the traveler. Rain was still heavy, so the exposed guest remained sheltered. A newly arrived traveler came in. At the settlement the water was unfit; the settlement, construed as PERSON, remembered. The child retained the corrected message. The guest received a gift, but left the house still carrying the old person's tool. Later the child repeated the message. The tale closes: a story may be left untold and the child still knows; a pledge breaks, and a path grows.
notes: Phase 2b guest-storyteller regression. Controlled traveler MOVE is ERG+A. When the newly arrived traveler remains discourse-prominent, the PERSON-like settlement is lexically reintroduced as kinatu rather than ambiguously resumed with ri. Testimony, hospitality, custody, and nested speech otherwise use ordinary grammar.
